tariff_note: Duty-free under the Canada-UK Trade Continuity Agreement. Without it, the UK tariff on natural honey is 16%.

compliance_requirements.name: Supplier's commercial document
compliance_requirements.detail: Since April 30, 2024 Canadian honey needs no CFIA health certificate for Great Britain: a commercial document completed by the supplier is enough. It's classed low-risk, so there are no routine border checks.

compliance_requirements.name: UK honey labelling (Honey (England) Regulations 2015)
compliance_requirements.detail: Reserved description 'honey', country of origin and the name and address of the UK food business operator.

compliance_requirements.name: CUKTCA origin declaration
compliance_requirements.detail: Self-declared origin statement on the invoice to claim 0% duty.

tax_note: Honey is zero-rated food for UK VAT (VAT Notice 701/14); any import VAT is handled by the UK importer.
notes: Lowest paperwork of any honey market in this set: no government certificate at all.

tariff_note: Duty-free under CPTPP as of the August 8, 2026 Japanese tariff schedule (the phase-out of the 25.5% WTO rate is complete).

compliance_requirements.name: Food Sanitation Act import notification
compliance_requirements.detail: The Japanese importer files an import notification with an MHLW quarantine station for each shipment.

compliance_requirements.name: Japanese food labelling
compliance_requirements.detail: Labels in Japanese under the Food Labeling Act, usually applied by the importer.

compliance_requirements.name: CPTPP certification of origin
compliance_requirements.detail: Self-certified by the exporter using the CPTPP minimum data elements. No official form.

tax_note: Consumption tax (reduced 8% food rate) is paid by the Japanese importer.
notes: Already Canada's #2 honey market: 29% of 2024 export volume, $19.8M (AAFC).

tariff_note: No tariff on honey (0% MFN), so CPTPP adds nothing on duty.

compliance_requirements.name: BICON bee-product import conditions
compliance_requirements.detail: Biosecurity conditions for bee products (manufacturer's declaration or inspection) must be met before food-safety checks apply.

compliance_requirements.name: Imported Food Inspection Scheme: surveillance food
compliance_requirements.detail: Honey is a surveillance food: 5% of consignments are referred for testing (C4 sugar adulteration, moisture, reducing sugars) and label review.

compliance_requirements.name: Food Standards Code labelling
compliance_requirements.detail: Labels must meet the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code.

tax_note: Any import GST is handled by the Australian importer.
notes: Australia is itself a large honey producer with strict biosecurity, so expect price competition and careful importer scrutiny.

tariff_note: Duty-free under CETA. Without it, the EU tariff on natural honey is 17.3%.

compliance_requirements.name: EU honey establishment listing (DG SANTE)
compliance_requirements.detail: The packing establishment must hold a Safe Food for Canadians licence and be on the EU's approved list for honey; request listing through the local CFIA office.

compliance_requirements.name: EU 'HON' export certificate via TRACES
compliance_requirements.detail: A CFIA inspector or veterinarian issues the model HON certificate in the EU's TRACES system for every consignment, before it leaves Canada.

compliance_requirements.name: Honey Directive 2001/110/EC composition and labelling
compliance_requirements.detail: Composition limits (moisture, HMF, sugars) and labelling rules, plus EU residue limits.

compliance_requirements.name: BPA-free food-contact packaging
compliance_requirements.detail: From July 20, 2026, primary packaging may not contain bisphenol A (Regulation 2024/3190).

compliance_requirements.name: CETA origin declaration
compliance_requirements.detail: Self-declared origin statement on the invoice to claim 0% duty.

tax_note: Import VAT (reduced 7% food rate) is paid and recovered by the German importer.
notes: Most honey enters Germany in 200 L drums for importers to blend and pack (CBI).

tariff_note: No Canada-China FTA: 15% MFN tariff on natural honey.

compliance_requirements.name: CIFER registration and GACC approval
compliance_requirements.detail: Licensed establishment gets a CFIA establishment ID, then registers and is certified in China's CIFER system before GACC approves its products (Decree 280 since June 1, 2026).

compliance_requirements.name: CFIA export certificate (CFIA/ACIA 2659)
compliance_requirements.detail: Request inspection and certificate from the local CFIA office; each honey lot must be graded first.

compliance_requirements.name: Registration number on packaging
compliance_requirements.detail: Inner and outer packaging must show the GACC registration number or CFIA establishment ID.

tax_note: Import VAT is paid by the Chinese importer.

tariff_note: 243% tariff: honey was excluded from tariff cuts under the Canada-Korea FTA, so the full MFN rate applies.

compliance_requirements.name: MFDS overseas facility registration
compliance_requirements.detail: The producing facility must be registered with Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety at least 7 days before import.

compliance_requirements.name: First-import laboratory inspection
compliance_requirements.detail: A product's first import into Korea goes through a detailed lab inspection before release.

compliance_requirements.name: CFIA export or free-sale certificate
compliance_requirements.detail: CFIA/ACIA 2659 (recommended for graded honey) or a Certificate of Free Sale (CFIA/ACIA 5786).

compliance_requirements.name: Korean-language labelling
compliance_requirements.detail: Korean labels applied before sale.

tax_note: Any import VAT is paid by the Korean importer.
notes: The tariff alone makes Canadian honey uncompetitive here despite the FTA.

tariff_note: 50% Section 338 tariff on Canadian natural honey (HTS 0409.00.00, heading 9903.03.14), in force since August 22, 2026, with NO CUSMA exemption.

compliance_requirements.name: FDA food facility registration
compliance_requirements.detail: The producing facility must register with the FDA before shipping food to the US, and renew every two years.

compliance_requirements.name: FDA Prior Notice
compliance_requirements.detail: Prior Notice must be filed with the FDA for every food shipment before it arrives.

compliance_requirements.name: Foreign Supplier Verification Program (FSVP)
compliance_requirements.detail: The US importer must verify the Canadian supplier's food safety controls; expect questionnaires and document requests.

compliance_requirements.name: US food labelling
compliance_requirements.detail: Labels must follow FDA format (Nutrition Facts, US units).

tax_note: No federal VAT; sold through a US importer, so the Canadian exporter doesn't collect sales tax.
notes: Took 68% of Canada's honey exports by volume in 2024 ($37.6M) — which is why the tariff hurts (AAFC).

status_note: Canada does not meet Mexico's requirements for exporting honey and apiculture products for human consumption. No CFIA certificate is currently available (CFIA).
tariff_note: Would be duty-free under CUSMA (20% without it), but the market is closed to Canadian honey.
